articles.title_orig: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Russian Refineries Again as Fuel Shortages Spread Across at Least 8 Regions
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Hits 2 Major Russian Refineries Again as Fuel Shortages Spread Across at Least 8 Regions
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Ukraine reportedly struck the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory for the second time this month. The wider campaign has cut Russian crude processing by 30% and contributed to gasoline shortages and sales restrictions in at least eight regions.
Ukraine attacked two major oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar Territory overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 18, marking the second strike on both facilities this month, according to Ukrainian monitoring channels and Russian media reports.
A large-scale drone attack targeted the Seversky District of the Krasnodar Territory.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Debris from the drones sparked fires at two industrial facilities, while fragments were found at nine other locations, including private residential yards and streets, the region’s operational headquarters reported. Four people were injured and are receiving medical attention.
The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ identified the facilities as the Afipsky and Ilsky oil refineries. Sources cited by the Russian independent outlet Astra also confirmed fires at both sites.
The Afipsky refinery is one of the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory and among the five largest in southern Russia. It can process more than 7 million tons of crude oil annually, producing gasoline, diesel fuel, jet fuel, and other petroleum products. The facility is focused exclusively on exports.
The Wednesday strike was the eighth attack on the Afipsky refinery since the beginning of the year and the second this month. It was last targeted by Ukrainian drones on Nov. 6.
The Ilsky refinery is also among the three largest in the Krasnodar Territory, with an annual crude oil processing capacity of approximately 6.6 million tons. It produces gasoline, diesel, and other petroleum products.
The facility was last targeted on Monday, when, according to Ukraine’s General Staff, three atmospheric crude distillation units were hit.
The Russian defense ministry said its air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones between 8 p.m. Moscow time on Tuesday and 8 a.m. on Wednesday.
According to the ministry, the drones were intercepted over the Belgorod and Rostov regions, Krasnodar Krai, Crimea, and the Sea of Azov.
Ukraine’s General Staff later confirmed that two oil refineries had been struck.
“Ukraine’s Defense Forces launched an aerial attack on the Ilsky and Afipsky oil refineries – two key fuel suppliers in southern Russia,” the General Staff said in a statement published on Telegram.
As per the report, explosions and smoke were observed near the Ilsky refinery, where storage tanks were hit.
Preliminary information indicates that an oil processing unit was struck at the Afipsky refinery. The facility has an annual processing capacity of 6.25 million tons, accounting for more than 2% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity.
The General Staff said the two refineries have a combined annual processing capacity of approximately 13 million tons of oil.
“Located in the south, they serve as the shortest supply route for fuel to Russian forces at the front. Therefore, every fire at these facilities means less diesel and gasoline for the Russian army, and fewer ‘oil-rubles’ – funds the Russian aggressor uses to purchase missiles and Shahed drones,” the statement said.
“Exercising their right to self-defense, as guaranteed by Article 51 of the UN Charter, Ukraine’s Defense Forces continue to take systematic measures to compel Russia to cease its armed aggression against Ukraine,” it added.
Kyiv resumed its campaign against Russian oil refineries in late October. Over the past few weeks, Ukrainian forces have struck around 10 of Russia’s 35 refineries, including facilities in Novokuibyshevsk, Ryazan, Afipsky, Saratov, Yaroslavl, Omsk, Nizhny Novgorod, Ufa, and Kirishi.
The attacks have contributed to a sharp decline in Russia’s oil refining volumes. Refineries were processing approximately 700,000 metric tons (5 million barrels) of crude oil per day at the end of October, but that figure had fallen to around 500,000 tons per day by mid-November – a reduction of about 30%, according to informed sources cited by Reuters.
The drop in refining capacity has also contributed to fuel shortages at gas stations in at least eight Russian regions, The Moscow Times reported .
Restrictions on gasoline sales have been introduced in the Leningrad, Nizhny Novgorod, Arkhangelsk, Novosibirsk, and Penza regions, as well as in the republics of Karelia and Buryatia.
In Moscow, Rosneft gas stations have reinstated purchase limits: Motorists can buy no more than 50 liters (13 gallons) of fuel per vehicle, while sales in canisters are capped at 20 liters.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

articles.title_orig: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.title_zh: I watched Trump, Xi and Putin gather in China. Here are my top takeaways
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.
China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers
Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition
Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.
But even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
Several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.
It was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.
Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.
"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.
During the tea break that followed, attendees quickly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.
They listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.
The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.
And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.
Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland .
Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

articles.title_orig: Xi, Putin blast Western 'protectionism' and sanctions as Trump lands in China
articles.title_zh: Xi, Putin blast Western 'protectionism' and sanctions as Trump lands in China
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Liz Lee, Laurie Chen and Jarrett Renshaw
SHENZHEN, China, Nov 18 (Reuters) - China's President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday to stand up against trade protectionism, but also gave a warm welcome to US President Donald Trump as he arrived ahead of a high-stakes trilateral meeting that will include the Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Xi greeted Trump at the airport, the first time he had done so with any visiting leader ‌since becoming president, reciprocating his counterpart's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September when they last met.
Trump's arrival came after Xi and Putin delivered pointed speeches ahead of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern ‌Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.
In his opening address, Xi urged support for what he called "free and open trade," trying to portray his country as a stable partner on the global stage, in contrast with the US, which has raised tariffs and taken a volatile approach to foreign policy under Trump.
In his ​speech, Putin criticised Western sanctions imposed over Russia's war in Ukraine.
At the Shenzhen airport, Xi and Trump briefly hugged and exchanged words before walking to their motorcades.
"China is a country of etiquette and has a tradition of reciprocating courtesy," Xi was quoted as saying by state news agency Xinhua. He added he was looking forward to discussing China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape.
Trump said every meeting with Xi has been "very pleasant," Xinhua reported.
They then joined Putin and other leaders at the APEC summit venue for handshakes, a group photo and a banquet.
The three men will meet on the sidelines on Thursday and potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US war in Iran, as well as other flashpoints such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.
A US official, and senior Russian ‌officials quoted by Russian news agencies, said Trump would also have a one-on-one meeting ⁠with Putin. The Russian officials said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned.
Russia's Interfax news agency cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov as saying that Putin and Xi discussed the trilateral meeting. Russian news agencies also quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying that one hour had been allocated for the three-way meeting.
The trilateral meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the ⁠US, Britain and the Soviet Union that formalised spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War Two order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
It has also unnerved some European and Asian capitals, which fear the world's greatest military powers will disregard their interests.
MESSAGE RESONATES WITH GLOBAL SOUTH
Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate.
"We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading ​system ​with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment," Xi told an audience of business executives.
Western trade partners ​have criticised China for running annual trade surpluses exceeding $1 trillion through policies that support its manufacturing ‌sector at the expense of its consumers.
Beijing says its growth model is appropriate for an economy still catching up with the world's richest, but Washington, Brussels and others are concerned about China's supply chain dominance providing the country with geopolitical leverage and say its policies threaten their industries and jobs.
Xi said China will continue to invest in its industrial complex and new technologies. The world's second-largest economy will lower tariffs and further open up its markets, while standing up against protectionism and unilateralism, he added.
His "message is likely to resonate with many Global South countries and reinforces Beijing's effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group.
Trump's trip to Asia is his first since his Republican Party's defeat in midterm elections this month, while allegations involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy add to the tension.
COLD RECEPTION FOR TAKAICHI
Leaders from Australia, Canada, South Korea and others were met by dancers and soldiers hoisting rifles, but ‌Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi landed without any welcoming ceremony.
Her visit to China comes amid a rift between Beijing and Tokyo that began a ​year ago after she said Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move on Taiwan also threatened its territory.
On Tuesday, Taiwan and Japan ​flagged incursions by Russian aircraft into their airspace.
Putin, who was speaking after Ukraine crippled the vital Kerch road bridge linking ​Crimea to Russia in a major blow to his four-year-old war, followed Xi on stage with a speech that described Western powers as "former hegemons."
He said Europe was in a "humiliating decline" and anti-Russian sanctions ‌imposed after his invasion of Ukraine had backfired.
"Experience has shown that the traditional tools of ​economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, ​having lost much of their intimidating power," Putin said.
"While sanctions, tariffs, and export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth—let alone crushing the economies of competitors."
In Manila, Trump vowed to deepen defence cooperation with the Philippines, amid its growing friction with Beijing over disputed features in the South China Sea. Earlier, he floated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, but that has not ​been confirmed.
The Kremlin this week dismissed comparisons with the Yalta Conference as "games of political scientists," ‌but said the meeting would have a major impact on global affairs. Beijing said the trilateral will promote world peace.
Putin described the world as "turbulent" but said disagreements can be addressed by "sitting at the table."
"I therefore expect ​big potential benefit from the upcoming trilateral meeting," he said.

articles.title_orig: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.title_zh: Hospitals Rush to Patch Java Vulnerabilities
articles.content_orig:
On November 17, 2026, details emerged exposing a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in OpenJDK, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (dubbed "Java4Shell") with a CVSSv4.0 score of 9.2. The bug exists in the optimized assembly code handling AVX-512 Base64 decoding, allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to cause heap memory corruption. Triggering this flaw on affected systems can lead to remote code execution.
The "Java4Shell" vulnerability and exploit were discovered and disclosed by security firm Calif.
CVE-2026-114938 is a memory-corruption vulnerability residing in the optimized Base64 decoding intrinsic engine of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). To maximize performance, OpenJDK uses an optimized implementation on supported x86-64 processors, based on AVX-512 VBMI instructions. However, the optimized assembly code miscalculates the output array bounds when handling inputs that contain an unexpected number of trailing padding characters (=).
When an input containing a specific sequence -such as 64 A characters followed by a single = - is parsed, the decoder's length calculation underflows to a negative value. This calculation mismatch causes an out-of-bounds write past the allocated heap memory buffer. Attackers can leverage this to overwrite adjacent object metadata, which can lead to code execution. We have proved that remote exploitation is feasible against standard Java applications such Jenkins, Confluence, and Apache Tomcat.
Like other memory safety issues, exploitation is possible with AI, but is not trivial. Our AI based vulnerability research harness, Wiz Atlas , managed to find and build a proof-of-concept exploit for this vulnerability within 2 hours, even before the full details were disclosed. Having said that, generalizing the exploit for an arbitrary target is difficult. We should expect adversaries to target commonplace Java applications, where specific builds and memory layouts repeat across targets. Motivated adversaries may tailor exploits with AI for specific targets, including home-grown applications.
Web Application Firewalls can help mitigate some of the exploits as they emerge in the wild. Since this vulnerability is rooted in OpenJDK itself, many possible code paths using user inputs may lead into the vulnerable code path, so it’s unlikely that WAF rules will be able to cover all possible paths, and will never be able to cover home grown applications completely. The best solution is upgrading to the latest OpenJDK version.
Prioritize externally facing, packaged Java applications, and make sure they are either patched or restricted from public access. Upgrade home-grown Java applications and update to the latest OpenJDK version containing the fix.
The vulnerability affects OpenJDK versions 17.0.6 and later, as well as downstream distributions, provided they run on x86-64 hardware supporting AVX-512 VBMI instruction sets (ARM64 processors are unaffected). Affected software distributions and hardware include:
OpenJDK Distributions: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, and Oracle Java SE (specifically versions 8u511b33-perf, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3).
Vulnerable CPU Architectures: Intel Xeon (Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids, Granite Rapids) and AMD EPYC/Ryzen (Zen 4 or newer).
Proven Vulnerable Applications (Pre-Auth RCE): Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, Keycloak, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and custom frameworks built on Spring Boot, Apache Struts, Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, Netflix Spinnaker and Apache Tomcat.
Security teams should immediately prioritize the following mitigation steps:
Audit and Patch: Identify all systems running OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later on AVX-512-capable x86-64 hardware. Apply the official security patches released on November 17, 2026, or update to downstream vendor-supplied builds immediately.
Verify Hardware Vulnerability: Run the following command on Linux systems to check if your infrastructure is physically affected:
If all four CPU flags are present in the output, the host runs the vulnerable hardware execution path.
Implement JVM Runtime Workarounds: If immediate patching is not possible, apply one of the following flags to JVM startup parameters to completely neutralize the vulnerability. They may have performance impact on the application.
Disable Base64 Intrinsics (Recommended): -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics
Disable AVX-512 execution (x86-64 only): -XX:UseAVX=2
Isolate Internet-Facing Services: Temporarily restrict external network access to vulnerable management portals (e.g., Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak) until mitigations or updates are deployed.
Wiz customers can use the pre-built query and advisory in the Wiz Threat Center to search for vulnerable instances in their environment.
On November 17, 2026 at 20:35 UTC, versions 1.26.1 & 1.26.2 of the Microsoft PyPI package agent-framework were published with an added credential stealer.  The package gets almost 200k downloads a month. The malicious versions have since been quarantined.

articles.title_orig: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.title_zh: Here’s how much Medicare Part B premiums are rising in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Medicare, which provides health insurance coverage to roughly 75 million retired seniors and disabled workers in the US, is getting more expensive next year.
Medicare Part B premiums, which cover doctors, outpatient care, some home healthcare services, and durable medical equipment, will rise about 3.2% to $209.40 a month in 2027, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced Tuesday .
That's an increase of $6.50 a month from $202.90 in 2026, bringing the total premium to $2,512.80 a year.
The Medicare Part B premium is deducted from your Social Security checks before you receive them. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 . Starting in January, the increase will add an average of $75 per month.
That is great news, but the Medicare premium increase will eat into it.
The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries increases to $292 in 2027, up $9 from $283 in 2026.
The increase in the standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending, according to CMS.
"The increase in the Medicare Part B premium for 2027 is less than the much steeper 10% increase in 2026, so that's a bit of good news," said Juliette Cubanski, director of the program on Medicare policy at KFF.
"Still, this increase comes on top of rising costs for other Medicare benefits, including prescription drugs, plus rising costs for other everyday essentials," she added.
Read more: How to add or adjust your Medicare coverage
People with traditional Medicare generally pay the Part B premium for physician coverage and a separate one for prescription drug coverage, known as Part D. Those premiums vary by plan. Some people pay an additional monthly premium for inpatient hospital coverage (Part A).
Each year, the Medicare Part B premium, deductible, and coinsurance rates are reset. If you're enrolled in traditional Medicare, you also have a Part D drug plan. The 2027 Part D base premium is $36 per month on average, but yours could be higher.
"Americans clearly understand that healthcare costs can threaten their retirement security," Kelly LaVigne, vice president of Consumer Insights at Allianz Life, told Yahoo Finance. But "so many don't fully understand what Medicare will and won't cover. And the details matter."
Roughly 15% of the average retiree's annual expenses will be health-related, according to Fidelity. On average, a 65-year-old who leaves the workforce this year may need $185,500 in savings to cover out-of-pocket healthcare expenses throughout retirement.
Even though the program offers fairly comprehensive coverage, traditional Medicare does not have an annual out-of-pocket limit.
The biggest hardship for many people enrolled in original Medicare is that Part B pays only 80% of expenses.
To cover the rest, you need to purchase a Medigap health insurance policy, sold by private insurers, that covers the remaining expenses.
For Medicare and Medicare Advantage users looking to make changes to their plans, the open enrollment period for 2027 ends Dec. 7.

articles.title_orig: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.title_zh: Costco sees surge in panic buying after string of tech outages, report says
articles.content_orig:
Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency-preparedness items in response to a recent string of technology outages , according to investment firm Mizuho Securities.
"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at Costco," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger wrote in a report.
Shoppers are "pantry-loading," while 21 of the retailer's 26 "high-ticket generators" were sold out online as of Sunday night, he added.
The recent outages, which blocked access to Microsoft apps , snarled flights nationwide and hindered banking activities at various times during the past week, are raising questions among Americans about a larger cybersecurity threat, CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman said on "CBS Mornings" on Wednesday.
The companies affected by the outages have said they were due to issues such as routine maintenance or upgrades, while the Federal Aviation Administration blamed its nationwide ground stop last week on a contractor updating its flight system.
"All of them have denied that cyberattacks are to blame," Gutman said. "Still, the system failures are fueling online speculation about a larger cyber threat."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that there's "zero evidence" that the recent outages in the U.S. are linked.
"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA . The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said during a news conference in the Philippines.
Costco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
The close timing of the outages highlights the country's increasing reliance on technology, John D'Arcy, a Temple University professor who researches cybersecurity and information technology failures, told CBS News Philadelphia.
"Our systems are so much more complex and so much more interconnected than they ever have been in the past, that when we just have one failure, the effects are much more dramatic," D'Arcy said.
The surge in panic buying could lift Costco's sales, Bellinger wrote. He raised his target price for the company's stock to $1,150 from $1,100. Other big-box stores, including Walmart and Sam's Club, could see similar "pantry-loading lifts," he added.

articles.title_orig: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China
articles.title_zh: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China
articles.content_orig:
House Democrats have demanded Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s son turn over years of Nvidia trading records, internal communications, and encrypted messages as they investigate whether the Trump administration’s China chip policy benefited the Lutnick family’s financial interests.
Reps. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), Gregory Meeks (D-NY) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Calif.) sent a five-page letter Tuesday to Brandon Lutnick , chairman of Cantor Fitzgerald, seeking records tied to the investment firm’s Nvidia-related holdings and business dealings in Southeast Asia.
The lawmakers are probing whether Howard Lutnick used his position to block restrictions on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company suspected of smuggling billions of dollars worth of restricted Nvidia AI chips to China.
“Did the Secretary of Commerce seriously and perhaps irreversibly compromise US national security interests to make money for his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald?” the lawmakers asked the younger Lutnick.
Howard Lutnick, who led Cantor Fitzgerald as chairman and CEO from 1996 until his confirmation in February 2025, transferred his ownership interests in the firm to trusts benefiting his adult children, Brandon and Kyle.
At the time of Lutnick’s confirmation, Cantor held more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares valued at over $1.3 billion, according to reports cited by the Democrats. The firm reduced its holdings by roughly 49% between September 2025 and March 2026, but still holds hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia stock.
The Democrats allege Lutnick’s resistance to adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department’s Entity List of companies banned from buying AI chips helped keep Nvidia’s stock price elevated while Cantor reduced its holdings.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has reportedly identified Lutnick as the primary obstacle to blacklisting Megaspeed, despite intelligence concerns that its CEO, Alice Huang, was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to compromise Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang through a romantic relationship.
Recently uncovered photos show Alice Huang cozying up to the Nvidia boss at dinners , drinks and technology events across Asia.
A former Commerce official told The Post last week that Lutnick refused to publish a proposed export-licensing rule in July 2025 despite other agencies approving the document.
The Democrats’ letter also raises questions about Cantor’s financial ties to Southeast Asian data centers that use Nvidia chips to serve Chinese customers, potentially circumventing US export restrictions.
The lawmakers want records of every Cantor trade involving Nvidia securities since January 2024, including transaction dates, quantities and the names of those responsible. They also want records of any actual or contemplated Nvidia investments held by President Trump and Howard Lutnick, as well as communications between Cantor and Commerce officials.
Notably, the Democrats want to know Cantor’s policies on encrypted and disappearing messages, as well as whether anyone involved in Nvidia trades or data center projects communicated with Commerce officials through Signal, WhatsApp or Telegram.
The Democrats also want records of Cantor’s business dealings in China and Southeast Asia dating back to January 2020, including investments, financing activities and regulatory approvals from Chinese government agencies.
Brandon Lutnick has until 5 p.m. Dec. 1 to produce the initial documents, with Raskin, Meeks and Kamlager-Dov also demanding the immediate preservation of emails, texts, encrypted messages and records stored on personal devices.
The Commerce and Justice departments said in a statement released Tuesday that the Megaspeed investigation began in 2024, with investigators requesting Nvidia sales records in May 2025 and interviewing Alice Huang the following month. The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation, reportedly after Nvidia’s general counsel contacted the Commerce Department seeking an update on the Megaspeed probe.
“We are confident that a full review of the facts will demonstrate that we have operated our business ethically and in full compliance with all applicable rules and regulations,” a Cantor Fitzgerald spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
The spokesperson also disputed claims that Cantor held a substantial proprietary position in Nvidia, saying its holdings primarily came from equity swaps executed for clients and shares purchased to hedge those trades. The reduction in those holdings reflected clients unwinding their positions, not Cantor independently deciding to sell, the rep claimed.
The firm also described its Southeast Asian data center ties as ordinary investment banking business, calling allegations that they influenced government decisions “baseless.”

articles.title_orig: William and Kate meet Indian Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi
articles.title_zh: William and Kate meet Indian Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi
articles.content_orig:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to reflect on the enduring ties between the UK and India, as they wrapped up their three-day visit to the country.
William and Catherine arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for the final leg of their first official overseas trip together in four years.
The meeting was a late addition to the couple's schedule and came after Modi confirmed he would be back from a scheduled trip to the Philippines in time to see the royals.
It comes a day after the royal couple were in Mumbai for the annual Earthshot Prize, which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects.
Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visit
A Kensington Palace spokesperson said the royals and Modi discussed the "strength and importance of the UKâIndia bilateral relationship, reflecting on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries and the opportunities to strengthen their partnership in the years ahead".
The prince and princess also spoke "warmly" of their time in the country, thanking the prime minister and the people for their welcome, and added how much they enjoyed returning to India, a decade after their last visit.
Modi called it a "pleasure" to meet them, and said he looks forward to "further strengthening" the India-UK partnership for the "shared prosperity of the people of our nations and the wider world".
The couple last met the Indian prime minister on their official visit to India in 2016.
When Prince William announced earlier this year that The Earthshot Prize ceremony was going to be held in India for the first time, he highlighted India's leadership in climate innovation, its biodiversity and its massive youth population as the key reasons for choosing the country.
Watch: William and Catherine attend Earthshot Prize in Mumbai
The royal spokesperson said that the meeting touched on the success of the ceremony in Mumbai, and India's "growing leadership in environmental innovation".
The event, founded by Prince William in 2020, was hosted this year by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.
The first engagement of their visit saw them play street cricket in Mumbai alongside cricket star Sachin Tendulkar, who holds the record for being the highest run scorer in international cricket.
William and Catherine's first official overseas trip in four years was short, but allowed them to combine personal projects - like Earthshot - with diplomacy.
As the future king and queen, they are viewed as a valuable diplomatic asset by the UK government.
And with Catherine recovering well and back on international duties following her cancer treatment, visits of a similar kind can be expected to fill their calendar.

With GTA 6 set to release on November 19, 2026, many fans have been wondering how long it will take to complete all of the trophies and achievements in the game in order to get the platinum or mythic achievements. Well, GTA 6’s story is going to be long, and its achievements are even more of a grind to get.
Obviously, it’s always somewhat difficult to predict exactly how long it will take to complete Grand Theft Auto 6 , as people have different skill levels; however, from what we’ve been able to gather from people who have actual knowledge of the game’s length, you’re looking at around 50 hours to complete the campaign with nearly 100 missions in total across five individual chapters ( first revealed in 2025 ).
Each mission will, of course, vary in length and take different players longer or shorter depending on their individual skills, but 50 hours seems to be the consensus average.
Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar Games , was interviewed by The New York Times, and here’s an interesting excerpt:
“I hope that there will be people that want to get up, have a cup of coffee, shower, get dressed, go out for a little exercise,” Nelson said. His 80-hour play-through of the game in February included the main story and some optional goals with narrative ramifications . Routines can escalate quickly. “Interact with some people, explore, maybe get into some trouble,” he added. “Rob some places, make some money.”
Also, don’t forget, you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here , if you haven’t already!
More Insider Gaming: All GTA 6 Platforms: PlayStation, XBOX, Nintendo & PC Status
This one is a little harder to predict than campaign completion in GTA 6, because some achievements and trophies could be considered RNG-based.
That said, based on what we’ve gathered, you’re probably looking at around 200 hours total to complete GTA 6; that’s more than double the time it takes to complete GTA 5. If you’re familiar with Red Dead Redemption 2, it’s probably a similar length and has been “officially” logged at 196 hours total to complete on average.
But again, in GTA 6’s case, it depends on some RNG-based elements for the trophies, similar to Red Dead Redemption 2’s “Zoologist and “Skip Deep” Trophies, such as scanning the 170 different wildlife species across the map , which was revealed in September 2026.

articles.title_zh: Hims & Hers launches new peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy
articles.content_orig:
Hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.
Even as it announced the new products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.
Hims in late October launched an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson said in a statement.
None of the company's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy."
The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.
The company will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.
Hims said it plans to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The company also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.
To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized plan to their needs, if appropriate.
The company said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.
"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options."
However, Vinjamoori said there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.
"We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he said. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a company of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead."
Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.
Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He said Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight."
But health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.
"With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body."
Kritzer said the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.
Without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide users, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.
Knoepfler said one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.
"With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?"
But he said the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.
That appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The company says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.
Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.
Hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.
In practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.
The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.
HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.
The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.
The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

articles.title_orig: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.title_zh: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
articles.content_orig:
In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.
The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.
Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.
If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.
So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?
In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.
He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.
Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track , and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.
Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.
Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.
But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.
Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".
Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.
She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.
Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.
She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.
The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.
Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.
He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.
Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.
He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".
Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.
Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.
Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.
He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.
Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.
Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.
He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.
His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.
Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.
But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.
Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.
He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.
The Canadian left the University of Toronto early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.
Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.
McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.
He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

articles.title_orig: Bank outage: How to protect your money when your bank goes offline
articles.title_zh: Bank outage: How to protect your money when your bank goes offline
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of Chase Bank customers reported they had trouble using their online accounts on Monday.
“JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug,” a spokesperson said Monday. “It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.”
The Chase spokesperson went on to say it was a “bug,” rather than a widespread cyberattack.
Social media users reported issues with transactions at physical Chase branches, as well, and some local bank branches told customers earlier in the day that they were having issues with their internal system. However, Chase said in a statement that “customers still have access to their accounts and funds.”
The outage wasn’t caused by a cloud-related issue or a cyber attack, a source familiar with the matter told CNN. Rather, an update on the company’s own physical computer systems inadvertently caused issues.
As of 2:00 p.m. ET, more than 4,700 customers reported issues with Chase, according to Downdetector.
Customers reported issues at other major banks, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and U.S. Bank, though on a smaller scale.
The reports with the other banks appear to be related to sending money through Zelle, a digital payment network, to Chase accounts.
“U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays,” U.S. Bank said in a statement.
Bank of America also said it was operating normally on Monday.
“Clients experiencing delays with other providers may wish to contact them directly for the latest information,” a spokesperson told CNN.
Zelle said that its service is “operating as it should.” The money-transferring service is owned by a consortium of US banks called Early Warning Services, and Zelle said it does not hold consumer funds.
“An issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers,” a Zelle spokesperson said.
Chase also said it wasn’t a systemic issue.
“Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us,” the spokesperson continued.
Monday’s Chase outage marked the third straight weekday with a massive technical failure.
On Thursday, a Microsoft outage cut off email access to millions of people across 74 countries and territories. On Friday, a Federal Aviation Administration systems failure led to a nationwide ground stop .
And on Monday afternoon, United Airlines reported a systemwide computer problem that delayed flights.
The incidents don’t share the same scope or root causes. Microsoft blamed a Windows defect, a traffic overload and capacity constraints. The FAA cited a router deployment issue and excessive data flooding its systems. It’s not yet clear what caused the Chase or United outages on Monday.
But the glitches share a common theme: “the complexity and fragility of the systems that we depend on every day,” Mike Chapple, a professor of IT, Analytics, and Operations at the University of Notre Dame, said in emailed comments.
“In each of these cases, what started as an issue in one small part of a larger system quickly spread, causing massive disruptions nationwide,” he added.
Complexity and interdependence aren’t inherently flaws — in fact, they make systems more resilient, noted Rebecca Krauthamer, CEO and cofounder of QuSecure, a cryptography provider for the US government.
“But when dependencies on systems aren’t sufficiently understood, failures can cascade across institutions and industries,” she added.
Think about it like the Titanic: The watertight bulkheads were unable to withstand a failure that exceeded the ship’s architects’ worst-case-scenario assumptions. Even the best-designed systems sometimes succumb to threats and problems that the designers couldn’t have imagined when they built them.
The problem with interdependent technology systems is that system failures are rarely isolated incidents: Our heavy reliance on a handful of systems means failures have tended to bring down systems across the world.
“The question for leaders is not whether one system will fail but how many other things fail with it, and how fast you can contain it,” said Madhu Shashanka, founder of Concentric AI.
This story has been updated with additional developments.
CNN’s David Goldman contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.title_zh: GTA 6: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S: Which Console Plays Best?
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here - and that means we can finally share the full details of how the game performs on each console platform: base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S.
We've already covered GTA 6's visuals in detail , focusing on the top-end experience on PS5 Pro, but the game's performance and fidelity can vary significantly depending on your platform of choice. The PlayStation and Xbox releases use different upscalers, for example, while the PS5 Pro release adds extra ray tracing effects. The Series S version is perhaps the most interesting of all, as it has to cram an extraordinary visual burden onto the weakest current-gen hardware - and more or less pulls it off, despite some noticeable cutbacks.
This article compares the game on every platform based on over 100 hours of testing across all four versions by John and Oliver, focusing on image quality, visual features and performance.
First, let's touch on resolution. The game runs at 2560x1440 (1440p) resolution on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X, with no immediate signs of dynamic resolution scaling.
On PS5 Pro, this is upscaled to 4K using PSSR, the Pro's bespoke AI temporal upscaler. PS5 and Xbox Series X instead get a spatial upscale to 4K using Rockstar's in-house TAA. The game therefore doesn't use temporal upscaling - such as QSSR on PS5 or FSR on Series X - and appears visually softer as a result. However, the decision does make sense .
The Series S is the odd one out here, with an internal resolution of 720p, temporally upscaled to approximately 1080p using FSR 4. From what we understand, this is the first shipping game on Series consoles to use the new upscaler .
All platforms target a 30fps frame-rate, a rarity for a current-gen game, but given the huge scale and intense simulation elements, the design makes sense . There's no option for a 40fps or 60fps mode on any platform.
As an aside, Xbox consoles can run the game in a 120Hz VRR container as an OS-level feature, which allows for a slightly smoother experience. PlayStation users don't have a 120Hz option, and while you can force VRR on, the system-level VRR only operates above 48fps and doesn't support low frame-rate compensation, so this does nothing in a 30fps title.
In terms of performance, the PS5 Pro offers the smoothest experience, with a consistent 30fps experience through around 75 hours of standard play in our testing. However, it is possible to experience short drops to a minimum of 24fps when destroying vehicles with the grenade launcher, but the frame-rate tends to recover quickly.
The base PS5 and Series X use the same 30fps target, but hold it a little more loosely, often flicking between 30fps and the high 20s during traversal, combat and other more challenging scenes. Returning to the same vehicle destruction hotspot, the frame-rate remains in the mid-30s while the carnage is unfolding, and only recovers when we leave the area. Again, it's possible for frame-rates to dip into the low 20s at the worst case.
Series S offers the loosest 30fps lock, with large portions of the game playing out at frame-rates from the mid to high 20s. Again, it's possible to depress the frame-rate to around 20fps with vehicular destruction. The other consoles do a credible job of hitting 30fps, but Series S often lies in a 25-30fps no-man's-land.
Note that, distinct from frame-rate, the game featured some animation update rate unsteadiness in pre-release footage (and our early testing on Xbox Series consoles). Thankfully, this long-standing RAGE engine issue seems to have been fixed in patches prior to launch, and animations now play out with consistent frame pacing.
Finally, input lag is similar to other Rockstar 30fps titles, like Red Dead Redemption 2. We measured around 180ms of end-to-end camera movement latency on Series X, including a wireless controller and around 10ms of display latency. This didn't seem to change substantially across 60Hz, 120Hz and 120Hz VRR. This is similar to RDR 2 and GTA 5 Enhanced, though input response is perceptually a bit better in GTA 6.
While all versions of the game - PS5, PS5 Pro, Series X, Series S - use ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) and ray-traced reflections, only the PS5 Pro version additionally supports ray-traced shadows. On other platforms, less consistent shadow maps are used, though these do support variable penumbra and have a high-resolution appearance.
Note that the RT reflections on all consoles are part of a hybrid approach, with screen-space reflections (SSR) layered in.
The Series S version is surprisingly feature-complete compared to the PS5 and Series X versions, supporting strand-based hair and the two RT effects, but it does come with some cutbacks. Most notably, lighting is lower precision overall and RT reflections are softer, lower-res and sometimes miss details. Shadows also appear visually degraded, with lower resolution shadowmaps and some absent cutscene self-shadows.
Additionally, driving at high speed through the game world results in more noticeable pop-in. Other minor downgrades include muddier textures at oblique angles, lower-res volumetric clouds, flatter water, lower-res hair and facial hair, and lower resolution depth of field effects.
Despite these necessary cutbacks, due to the Series S console's more limited memory and cut-down GPU, the overall visual feature set is still similar to Xbox Series X and PS5. Thankfully, the full-fat CPU and SSD on the Series S mean that the scale and scope of Leonida isn't affected.
It's worth bearing in mind that the nature of the game make it hard to nail down absolutely every change, especially as John played only on PS5 and PS5 Pro, while Oliver played only on Xbox Series X and Series S. We'll have more direct cross-platform comparisons in future content.
In terms of visual features and performance, the PS5 Pro version is the best option available, with solid frame-rates, 4K-like image quality and a noticeable visual upgrade thanks to ray-traced shadows. However, the game looks and plays well on base PS5 and Xbox Series X as well, despite occasional minor frame-rate drops during regular play and a softer 1440p image. The Series S version of the game is the hardest to recommend, with consistent frame-rate drops to the mid-20s, a 1080p output resolution and a long list of visual cutbacks, though the overall character of the game's visuals still shines through.
For more, why not read our full GTA 6 tech review ?

articles.title_orig: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.title_zh: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Bill Gurley , the venture capitalist behind an early bet on Uber ( UBER ), has an idea for how Google could slow Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) down: Give the AI away.
Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google should use free AI to keep Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) from pulling away. Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday and begins trading Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT .
"If Google recognizes that Anthropic ... and OpenAI maybe are getting escape velocity away from them, it is the No. 1 thing they should go do ... bar none," he said.
Gurley calls it playing defense. Open-weight models, which anyone can download, run and change for free, keep one company from locking up a market. Google did it with Kubernetes "when they were worried about Amazon and AWS," he said, and with Android "when they were worried about Apple having a monopoly in phones."
The catch? "We're not seeing those actions from Google."
Free models already do most of the work. On OpenRouter, a marketplace developers use to reach hundreds of AI models, seven of the 10 most-used models last week came from Chinese labs and are free to download. DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash alone processed about 77 trillion tokens, the basic units of text that AI models read and write. That's more than the other nine combined.
Duolingo ( DUOL ) CEO Luis von Ahn told Yahoo Finance last week that open models cut the cost of each AI video call to less than a cent from about 30 cents. "The vast majority of our usage of AI will be in open-weight models pretty soon," he said.
The money flows the other way. Closed models handled 28% of OpenRouter's tokens in mid-September but collected 73% of the spending, according to its September report . Similarly, Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone accounted for about a fifth of phones sold in the second quarter but generated nearly half of revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.
Price is a big reason. Anthropic lists Claude Opus 5.5, its most-used model, at about 27 times what DeepSeek charges for its own. And while 39 companies sell DeepSeek's model on OpenRouter, nobody sells Claude Opus for less than Anthropic does. As Gurley put it, "The marginal price is going to equal marginal cost."
Gurley also called Anthropic's choice to write off model training costs right away, rather than over years, "pretty amazing," adding, "it's still profitable, really high gross margin."
"Anthropic — just reading through the S-1 — I think it's the most impressive business I've ever reviewed," Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, said on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Friday.
OpenRouter tracks developers, not the ChatGPT or Claude apps. And Android cut both ways. It protected Google, but Apple kept collecting.
Gurley's worry is Washington. He said Anthropic's lobbying effort is "probably unprecedented for a company of their age or size," and he sees it as a push for regulatory capture , meaning rules shaped by the companies they govern. In AI, that could mean rules that favor closed labs over open models.
He still gives Anthropic its due. "It is remarkable what they've done," he said. "I tip my hat to them. I just wish they weren't lobbying so hard."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before Senate banking committee, Chairman Scott says
articles.content_orig:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott , R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded.
"They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas."
Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate.
A spokesperson for the banking committee did not immediately respond to questions about when Huang and Lutnick would testify. In initial letters to the pair, Scott requested Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10.
Scott said the appearances will provide the committee with "more information about what they knew, when they knew it and why they didn't do something about it."
"Nvidia seemed to have fairly lax controls, and I want to know how much of the relationship with Alice [Huang] impacted Nvidia's unwillingness or inability, or frankly, just blindness to Megaspeed's providing access to China of the most advanced chipset," Scott said of Jensen Huang's testimony.
The outgoing banking committee chair also homed in on Lutnick, calling for answers as to why the commerce secretary did not act after being warned about Megaspeed — the Singaporean company where the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive. Nvidia sold its chips to Megaspeed, which U.S. investigators suspect of diverting them to China.
"They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the 'entity list,'" Scott said, referring to a Commerce Department list of companies the U.S. views as national security risks. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security "didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why."
Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have been embroiled in an intra-administration battle as the fallout from the Huang affair grows. Bessent on CNBC on Friday appeared to blame Lutnick for a lack of action on Megaspeed.
"You will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said, referring to Commerce and noting his department has long supported imposing restrictions on Megaspeed.
A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott's announcement that he has agreed to appear.
Huang's upcoming appearances are likely just the start of the embattled former CEO's problems on Capitol Hill. Democrats will take control of Congress in January and have demanded sweeping investigations into the affair and Huang's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump .
The House Energy and Commerce Committee asked interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress for a briefing no later than Dec. 2 on the company's chip exports and information about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. The panel also asked Lutnick and a top deputy to appear to discuss chip export controls. The Wall Street Journal first reported the letters to Kress and Lutnick, and a committee spokesperson confirmed the report to CNBC.
— Megan Cassella and Ashlee Trujillo contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.title_zh: 10 Features That Surprised Me While Playing GTA 6 On Xbox Series X
articles.content_orig:
Copies of GTA 6 are beginning to arrive, with one difference spotted between the Xbox and PlayStation versions.
Grand Theft Auto VI ’s November 19 launch is almost finally upon us, with copies of the game already in the hands of many.
Preloads for digital copies of the game began on November 10 after Rockstar Games shifted the date forwards due to the title’s enormous file size .
For those who opted for code-in-a-box copies, preloads open today, on November 12.
Those who have a code-in-a-box copy in hand have taken to social media to reveal that the box features a double-sided fold-up poster, which is a nice touch.
One side features Lucia, with GTA VI ’s key art appearing on the other; the Grand Theft Auto franchise’s classic art style is used.
What has now been realised, however, is that those with an Xbox code-in-a-box copy are getting a slight downgrade compared to their PlayStation counterparts.
X (formerly Twitter) user GameRiot took to the site to share that “the GTA VI poster is actually smaller on Xbox compared to PS5”.
You can see in the video clip below that we’re not talking a couple of milimetres here.
There is likely a very good reason for this, as GameRiot points out, and that’s all down to case sizing.
While PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S physical cases are similarly sized, it appears that the area for posters, booklets, and such like within the Xbox case is slightly smaller.
Therefore, GTA VI ’s poster has been made smaller to fit accordingly, rather than this being any form of intentional slight to Xbox users.
It may feel that way amid Rockstar Games and PlayStation’s ongoing “plays best” marketing campaign that favours Sony’s console.
What isn’t abundantly clear yet is whether this difference in poster sizing is worldwide or whether this is unique to where GameRiot is based in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto fans are definitely seeing the humour in this latest spot.
“Cancelled my pre-order, unplayable,” joked BanksniO.
“They taking plays best on PS5 too seriously,” added vce_bby.
It’s a shame that Jason doesn’t get the chance to shine on the poster, unless he’s going to pop up elsewhere.
GameRiot did confirm that the PS5’s poster is roughly A3 sized while Xbox’s is understandably somewhat below A3 which could make the Xbox version difficult to frame, if that’s something you’re interested in.
READ MORE: GTA 6's first player ratings surface early via PlayStation Store, oops
It’s definitely been a busy week for GTA VI with an endless stream of marketing continuing to rollout.
Rockstar Games announced GTA VI : The Festival , a once-in-a-lifetime launch party based in Miami, Florida, plus Metacritic and Fandom have revealed a contest where you could win up to $500 in Visa gift cards simply by predicting GTA VI ’s Metacritic score .
We’ve also had confirmation that GTA VI will only run at 30fps , including on the PlayStation 5 Pro - something that’s ruffled a few feathers.
If you haven’t preloaded your game already, you may want to this weekend. GTA VI will be here before you know it.
